extra.WP-31:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 148 from WP-28] WP-29 already documented the new fields in docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md. The OQ-configuration-model-20 part of this request is #149 (docfix), and the repository-layout Markers part is #150 (docfix). For docs 09, 10 and 11, document WP-28's committed shapes. Circuit breaker (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-5 (a)): minimumLegs 20, failureRatio 0.5 (0 to 1), halfOpenSuccesses 3. Schema defaults (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-6): circuitBreaker maxConnections 1024 (in-flight attempts per Upstream per Node), maxPendingRequests 256, consecutiveFailures 5, openDuration 30s; healthCheck.passive consecutiveErrors 5 and ejectionTime 30s; healthCheck.active path /, interval 10s, timeout 2s, healthyThreshold 2, unhealthyThreshold 3; endpoints[].weight 1; loadBalancing.algorithm least-request; retries.attempts 1. Gateway stateStore.cache = {topology (default standalone), url (required secret)}: always redis, with no timeout of its own, so cache Policies default to stateStore.timeout (OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-3 (a)); the ratelimit localOnly text follows OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 (a). telemetry.otlp.tls uses the Upstream tls shape (sni, caCertificate, clientCertificate, clientKey; certificate and key both or neither) for OQ-observability-2 (a). Also document the endpoint pattern ^https?://[^/?#@\s]+/?$, amend the Observability Scope sentence that lists 'three telemetry fields', and give traceSampling its default of 0.01.
- [CR 52 from WP-09] Add an Open questions row to docs/architecture/10-observability.md (next free number, OQ-observability-22 at this writing) and cite it from the 'Overhead per signal' metrics memory paragraph. Figures from WP-09's BenchmarkCollect125k (spec 09 test 46, risk 1): at S = 8 and 125,743 series, live heap is 33.3 MiB against the modelled ~22 MiB (8.3 MiB aggregates + 8.3 MiB collection + 5.4 MiB striping). The overrun is in the aggregates: 25.5 MiB against a modelled 13.7 MiB, including the handles and plans of both bound Revisions and one attribute.Set per label set. The pooled collection is about 7.8 MiB, under the model, and the heap does not grow with a fifth reader (33.64 vs 33.65 MiB). Note that 'All telemetry' then exceeds the 40 MiB telemetry live-heap seed adopted in OQ-observability-17 (a). Options: (a) adopt the measured figure and revisit the seeds with Performance budgets; (b) cut aggregate overhead, for example by building attribute sets at collection or sharing plans between bound Revisions; (c) lower admission limits or the retiring ceiling.
- [CR 111 from WP-22] In docs/architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md 'Load balancing', replace 'all build at v = 244, about 238 MiB (hypothesis)' with 'all build at v = 245, about 239 MiB (hypothesis)'. The normative formula with no round-robin schedules gives floor((256 MiB − 16 MiB) ÷ (16 B × 64,000)) = floor(245.76) = 245, and 245 × 16 B × 64,000 = 250,880,000 B ≈ 239.3 MiB. The code pins 245 in TestPlanBudgetFormula (internal/gateway/upstream/balance/budget_test.go:41). Spec 05 test plan item 11's 'v = 244' has the same error.
- [CR 112 from WP-22] In TMR 'Load balancing', make the schedule and ring sizing explicit so that they do not imply n_i = max(1, round(w_i × L / Σw)). That formula need not sum to L: 2,000 equal Endpoints would give 66,000 slots, above the 256 KiB maximum. Quotas are apportioned to sum exactly to the structure size; each Endpoint of weight above 0 gets at least one slot, and every quota is within one slot of its rounded share unless the at-least-one floor forces extra slots elsewhere. Weight-0 Endpoints get no slots (quotas() in internal/gateway/upstream/balance/endpoint.go). This supersedes the n_i wording of spec 05 reqs 12 and 14.
- [CR 32 from WP-06] WP-63 (cache Filter, 05 req 79): this rule applies on a Route whose effective chain holds an auth-class Policy and whose cache config has no config.key. A request whose filter.Identity.Principal is "" (an unbound token without a string sub, or an unbound certificate with an empty subject) MUST bypass both lookup and store, counted as ruralz_cache_requests_total{result="bypass"}. Never use "" as a partition there, because it would share entries across clients and issuers. On Routes without an auth-class Policy, the partition stays "" as req 79 says. Treat Principal as an opaque string (it may hold a percent-encoded iss) and never rebuild it from iss and sub. Unsafe-method invalidation (05 req 85) is keyed by URI generation, not partition, and still runs. WP-31: in docs/architecture/09-traffic-management-and-resilience.md, extend the Response caching 'Principal' row: an authenticated request without a principal bypasses the cache (OQ-security-and-identity-32, which the lead records in doc 08).
- [Minor 17 from WP-09] internal/telemetry/aggregate counts retiring listener and enumeration-only series against the 25,000 retiring ceiling but never folds them (09 req 55), so once retiring listener series alone exceed the ceiling the exported ruralz_telemetry_series{state="retiring"} stays above it with nothing left to fold (about 243 retiring listeners at production scale). docs/architecture/10-observability.md 'Cardinality budget' says 'beyond it the oldest retiring sets fold': add that listener sets never fold and can exceed the ceiling, or record an OQ-observability row.
- [Minor 83 from apply-2] docs/architecture/08-security-and-identity.md 'Pre-authentication throttling' proposes to Observability per-cause refusal counters for the three RZ-AUTH-007 causes (hash-queue overflow, bucket-creation cap, delay overflow). docs/architecture/10-observability.md lists only ruralz_auth_decisions_total{policy,result,code}. Record this as an OQ-observability row with options (for example (a) a cause label or a new counter in the auth group; (b) none, the code label suffices). A metric can be added only together with an internal/telemetry/catalog change that the lead approves.
